holes.notes: Identified by registering the club banguide to the world frame: I detected all 18 red flags in the guide, traced each flag-pole foot to the green, and RANSAC-fitted a similarity transform against the 17 OSM green centroids. 16 of 17 matched with mean residual 1.5 m / max 2.7 m (scale 1.5296 banguide-px per metre, rotation 0.08 deg, i.e. the banguide is north-up). Hole 1's orange disc (the tee marker) lands at world (-5.3,-172.5) beside the clubhouse (OSM 'Upsala golfklubb' building at (16,-280)); its drawn line runs SE and ends on the flag whose pole foot converts to (275.8,66.3) - OSM green w452926949 / label G9 at (276.0,66.2), a 0.3 m agreement, so the green assignment is certain. Confirmed independently on the z18 imagery: the green sits on the north shore of the pond with the two OSM greenside bunkers w438979741 (257,61) and w452928633 (290,60) flanking it exactly as drawn. Hole plays 371 m (par 4) SE at bearing ~126-134 deg, essentially straight with a very slight left bow (the guide's drawn line passes (121,-81), ~15 m north of the tee-green chord). Three fairway bunkers at (158,-42),(164,-26),(177,-27) sit roughly 200 m out in the right half of my traced corridor and confirm its line. CAVEAT: the tee pads are the weakest part. This corridor is on Esri summer imagery whose resolution here is ~0.5 m; at the disc position there is a levelled, walled platform plus a sandy patch around x -10..+12, z -196..-170 that reads as a tee complex, but I could not resolve individual pads, so tee rectangles are placed on the disc and the platform (±10 m) rather than traced. Fairway edges are a 40-54 m corridor fitted to the visible mowing bands; the spring/summer imagery seam crosses this hole near x=50 and makes the mowing boundaries hard to read, so the edges are approximate (±10 m). Water is OSM pond w35415026-neighbour w35415031 (6613 m2, my simplification 6678 m2), which crosses the approach ~60 m short of the green and fronts the putting surface from the south.

Short par 3, 148 m, playing NNW (bearing ~340 deg). Identified from the banguide: the '2' disc sits at world (320.5,30.0), only 46 m from hole 1's green, and its line runs north to the flag whose pole foot converts to (270.9,-110.0) - OSM green w452926956 / label G16 at (270.2,-109.7), 0.7 m agreement. Assignment is certain. Confirmed on imagery: the green reads as a darker irrigated oval with the big OSM bunker w438979717 (267,-87, 180 m2) tucked front-left, exactly the arrangement the guide draws. CAVEAT on the tee: at the disc there is a smooth, slightly darker mown platform spanning roughly x 310-340, z 0..38 which is clearly the tee complex, but at ~0.5 m effective ground resolution I could not separate individual pads, so the two rectangles are modelled on that platform (back tee at the far/high-z end) rather than traced - position good to ~8 m, size and angle inferred. FAIRWAY: a par 3, so there is no true fairway; I supplied a narrow (30-36 m) mown approach strip running from ~35 m in front of the tee to the green front, which is where the imagery shows smoother, greener turf. Treat that ring as low-confidence and drop it if the pipeline prefers par 3s bare. No water in play - the nearest pond, OSM w438964102 at (308,-201), lies ~90 m beyond the green and is not a hazard on this hole.

Best-evidenced of the three. The '3' disc converts to world (386.0,-127.2) and lands squarely on a smooth mown tee oval visible in the z18 imagery at x 380-401, z -130..-108, with a second (forward) tee oval 37 m down the hole at x 399-417, z -96..-80 - independent confirmation that the banguide registration is good to a few metres. The drawn line runs due south to the flag whose pole foot converts to (430.2,194.4) - OSM green w452926944 / label G4 at (430.2,193.4), 1.0 m agreement. I verified the OSM outlines against the imagery by overlay: green ring, the two left-front bunkers w438986830 (408,200) and w438986828 (419,206), the big right bunker w438986825 (449,203) and the lake shoreline all land exactly on their features, so the green ring here is trustworthy. 320 m par 4 playing south (bearing ~170-178 deg). The corridor is a genuine strip of land between two waters: OSM lake w35415026 (9714 m2) runs the whole right/east side from z=-15 to the green, and the east lobe of pond w35415031 squeezes the left/west side from z=100 to 175; the fairway narrows to ~40 m between them. Fairway ring traced from the clear pale mown band, with the east edge held 2-4 m inside the surveyed shoreline; a left fairway bunker, OSM w438981573 at (378,132), sits on that traced west edge and confirms it. Only real uncertainty is where the fairway begins: from the tee to about z=-40 the ground is heath/bare with scattered trees, so I started the ring at z=-25, an 85-100 m carry - defensible but read by eye.

Identified on the banguide: disc 4 sits ~49 m W of the 3rd green (the red flag by the big east lake) and its line sweeps WNW along the SW shore of the middle pond, then turns N to a green. I fitted a 7-point affine banguide-px -> world (residuals 2-15 m, <7 m everywhere in this NE corner) from the two east lakes, the south pond and four confidently matched greens; hole 4's drawn pin lands at (87.8,-49.2), i.e. 4.1 m from OSM green G13 (83.7,-48.7), so the assignment is certain. Drawn length along the club's own curve ~393 m (straight tee-green 380 m) - a long par 4. Fairway = the pale dormant corridor between the pond (right/NE) and the conifer belt (left/SW), with its NE edge clipped to stay >=12 m off OSM pond w35415031. OSM stream w306287293 crosses the approach ~90 m short of the green (given as the 4 m wide 'ditch'). TEES ARE THE WEAK PART: spring imagery with long conifer shadows over the tee shelf, no individual pads resolvable at 0.3 m/px even after gamma lift; the two pads given sit on the smooth open turf at the banguide disc (381,190), which is where a next tee belongs. NOTE the four OSM tee pads at (388-437, 292-313) are NOT this hole's - they go with OSM green G1 (407.6,352.6) in a woodland clearing that the banguide fades out entirely, i.e. a separate loop/practice hole.

Par 5, dogleg right. On the banguide the line starts at disc 5 (~100 m S of the 4th green, just S of the ditch), runs almost due S for ~250 m, then bends right into a broad open bowl and finishes W at a green whose plotted pin is 21 m from OSM green G2 (-42.3,466.8) - by far the nearest green, and the 6th tee sits immediately WSW of it, exactly as the banguide shows. The z18 imagery confirms the whole route: a 35-45 m corridor between two conifer belts down to about z=290, then a wide mown bowl swinging W to G2 with its four bunkers. Drawn centreline 485 m (straight tee-green 445 m). Fairway ring traced from the pale dormant turf; its eastern half of the bowl is hole 5's, the western half of the same open bowl is shared with the 17th/18th and is deliberately left out. Water: the small 200 m2 OSM pond w439464398 sits ~50 m right of the tee. A second pond (OSM w439048474, centre approx -114,425) lies ~80 m NW of the green inside the woods - visible but not in play, so omitted. Tees: two pads read as the greener, smoother rectangles at (104,46) and (96,60) - medium confidence on the exact pad outlines, high on the tee END location (the banguide disc plots at 109,48).

Long par 3 (~192 m) playing due W. On the banguide it is a single short straight line from disc 6 (immediately SW of the 5th green) to a green drawn with two white bunkers and a pond right below it - exactly the picture the satellite shows at OSM green G5 (-317.3,519.1): two bunkers short/N of the green and OSM pond w221190914 guarding front-right. The banguide affine over-reaches in this far-south corner (its plotted pin lands 34 m ENE of G5, and its 5th pin 21 m ENE of G2), so I did NOT use the disc position (-93.7,523.8) for the tee - that point falls in trees. Instead the tees are put on the mown tee shelf that is actually visible in the imagery, a smooth uniform green band at x -170..-115, z 499..513, with a distinct 15x8 m oval at about (-133,505). Back tee taken as (-127,506) -> 192 m to the green centre; if the club plays it from further back the imagery gives no room, the mown ground ends at x approx -112 where the conifers start. The 'fairway' ring is the continuous mown through-turf strip between the tee and the pond, which reads as fairway-height in the imagery; on a par 3 you may prefer to demote it to first cut. Confidence medium only because of the tee-position shift and because the hole is long for a par 3 - the identification of the hole and its green is otherwise unambiguous.

IDENTIFICATION (certain): I detected all 18 red flags, all 17 numbered discs and every drawn hole line in the banguide as separate connected components, then walked each line to see which disc it joins to which flag. Hole 7 = the line from orange disc '7' (banguide px 669,1730) to the red flag at px (418,1098). GEOREFERENCING: the banguide is north-up; a similarity fit from 14 flag-centroid <-> OSM-green-centroid pairs gives 0.6532 m/px, rotation 0.03 deg, residuals 0.2-1.7 m, so banguide pixels convert to world metres essentially exactly. Under that fit flag(418,1098) -> (-428.7,53.5), i.e. OSM green G0 at (-428.5,52.4), residual 1.1 m -> greenOsmIndex 0 is certain. GREEN RING is SYNTHESISED, not traced: in this vivid-summer half of the imagery the putting surface is tonally identical to its apron and no edge could be found (region-grow ran away to 1250 m2). I fitted a 523 m2 oval on the OSM centroid, sized to sit between the two OSM greenside bunkers at (-410.7,59.1) east and (-436.6,69.9) south-west, whose bright sand edges I could locate (east bunker starts at x=-413). Use the OSM outline in preference. FAIRWAY traced from a mown-turf classification (green ratio > 0.44, low texture) with perpendicular cross-sections every 40 m, half-widths median+mean smoothed, capped at 45 m: the hole is a narrow chute of 10-20 m mown width for the first ~130 m out of the tee (dense pine belt on the west, treeline on the east), then opens to a 40-55 m fairway that runs NNW to the green. One fairway bunker (OSM w..., centroid -384.3,259.7) sits in the left half of the corridor. TEES are the weak point: the guide disc centre maps to (-264.5,466.3) which in the satellite is dry rough under scattered pines. The only tee-shaped feature within 40 m is a smooth mown strip aligned 342 deg running x -297..-286, z 451..483, hemmed on its west by the cart-path loop that also serves the 6th green; I placed both pads on it. This moves the tee 25 m WSW of the guide disc and changes the hole length by only 5 m (449 m vs 444 m straight). NO WATER on or beside this hole - the three dark blobs my water detector flagged inside the crop are conifer shadow, verified by eye. Centerline 451 m along the corridor, so this plays as a par 5.

IDENTIFICATION (certain): banguide line component running from orange disc '8' (px 277,1050) to the red flag at px (829,549); under the 14-point similarity fit that flag maps to (-160.5,-305.3), i.e. OSM green G7 at (-159.1,-306.0), residual 1.6 m -> greenOsmIndex 7. GREEN RING is a genuine trace: colour region-grow from the OSM centroid on a z18 crop gives 480-515 m2 with centroid (-161.0,-309.1), 3.6 m from the OSM centroid and area consistent with OSM's 545 m2 - an independent confirmation of the assignment. FAIRWAY: the guide's drawn line is a smooth curve that CUTS ACROSS the double pond between about 190 m and 260 m from the tee; the real mown corridor passes to the pond's NORTH-WEST. I therefore refit the corridor axis to the mown mask (first pass) and re-extracted the ring about that axis, then extended it through the approach to the green edge by hand off the z18 crop, and resampled the ring to 20 points. The corridor is a clean 40-55 m band from the SW corner of the property, up the west side of the open ground, past the pond on its left, then NE to the green; a bunker sits front-left of the green at (-190,-310) (OSM has one at -111,-334.9 only). WATER: the feature is one pond crossed by a sand causeway/cart path, so I give it as two lobes: west 1433 m2 (x -394..-332, z -175..-109) and east 857 m2 (x -348..-301, z -145..-81). Both are hard against the right of the fairway and are the defining hazard of the hole. There is a third, larger pond at (-310,-320) north-west of the approach but it belongs to holes 12/13, so I left it out. TEE is the weak point: the guide disc maps to (-520.9,22.2), which in the satellite is scrub and long tree shadow at the SW corner of the course - no pad is resolvable at 0.30 m/px there, so I placed a single pad at the guide position and set angDeg 41 (bearing to the fairway centre at 200 m). Centerline 499 m along the corridor: a par 5.

IMPORTANT - THE BRIEF'S ASSUMPTION IS WRONG: hole 9 does NOT return to the clubhouse. Its tee is ~160 m NW of the clubhouse and it plays 360 m NE, AWAY from it, to a green tucked in a tree pocket at the far NE of the western block; the 10th tee is then 139 m from the 9th green. The clubhouse pair is 1 and 18 (18th green G11 at -8.4,-123.7, 1st tee 16 m away). I verified this by extracting every drawn hole line as a connected component and walking each from its numbered disc to its flag: the 18 lines form one closed rotation, every green->next-tee walk is 16-139 m (median 84 m), so the routing is not in doubt. Full routing recovered (tee -> green, world m): 1 (-11.5,-139.4)->G9; 2 (314.0,62.9)->G16; 3 (379.2,-93.9)->G4; 4 (374.2,223.5)->G13; 5 (95.8,80.6)->G2; 6 (-119.5,538.7)->G5; 7 ->G0; 8 ->G7; 9 ->G15; 10 (151.1,-358.4)->G6; 11 (~290,-514)->G14; 12 (-13.0,-574.5)->G3; 13 (-406.0,-203.9)->G8; 14 (-126.0,-471.2)->G10; 15 (-115.4,-211.9)->G12; 16 (-372.6,50.9)->green at (-216.9,423.1) NOT IN OSM; 17 (-189.4,502.1)->green at (-57.0,229.0) NOT IN OSM; 18 (-136.0,258.5)->G11. So all 17 OSM greens are consumed and holes 16 and 17 are the two with no OSM green. IDENTIFICATION of hole 9: line from orange disc '9' (px 926,622) to the flag at px (1337,257) -> (171.2,-496.2), i.e. OSM green G15 at (171.7,-495.4), residual 0.9 m -> greenOsmIndex 15. GREEN RING is a genuine trace (region grow on a z18 crop): 563 m2, centroid (170.7,-495.5), 1.2 m from the OSM centroid and matching its 550 m2 - strong independent confirmation. FAIRWAY traced from a fairway-tone classification over the big open field; ~55 m wide, running NE. It stops at x~130 because a conifer strip at x 125..155, z -505..-455 separates the fairway from the green complex - the approach has to carry or skirt it. Two OSM bunkers short-left of the green at (155.9,-504.3) and (147.0,-513.2). WATER: pond at (-13,-484), 423 m2, about 30 m beyond the fairway's left edge; it most likely serves hole 11 or 12 as well, listed here because it is visibly beside this corridor. A second dark blob I checked at (135,-482) is conifer shadow, not water. TEE: the guide disc maps to (-97.1,-257.6), which IS mown turf, but no distinct pad is resolvable at 0.30 m/px, so the pad size/shape is nominal; angDeg 24 is the drawn line's initial bearing (the hole then bends right to an overall 48 deg). The two OSM bunkers 20-35 m ENE of the tee at (-81.3,-262.3) and (-68,-231) belong to the clubhouse short-game/practice area (the OSM driving range polygon starts just south at z=-220), not to hole 9. Centerline 387 m: a long par 4.

Identified from the banguide: disc 10 sits at the SW end of a straight white line running NE to a red flag whose pole base lands on OSM green G6. I georeferenced the banguide by fitting a scale+translate (0.652 m/px, no measurable rotation; world_x=(px-1066.6)*0.652, world_z=(py-1058.3)*0.652) to three flag/green pairs, and it reproduces G6, G14, G15 and G3 to 2-6 m, plus an independent check: a dark maintenance building the guide shows at world (87..118,-375..-344) is on the satellite at (100..121,-378..-355). Hole 10 is a PAR 3 of ~171 m playing NE (bearing 43 deg) from a tee just north of OSM scrub w439045878 up to G6, which sits ringed by OSM bunkers b49 (front-left), b48 (front-right), b50/b51 (rear). My own trace of the putting surface off a 0.075 m/px crop agreed with the OSM ring to 2-3 m, so I return the OSM ring as the fallback. NO FAIRWAY RING: the ground between tee and green reads on the satellite as unmown tan sandy heath/scrub (OSM tags scrub over x 88-192, z -470..-396 at the tee end), not mown turf; the only mown surface I can resolve is the apron immediately around the green, which I cannot separate from the green's own fringe at this resolution. TEE IS THE WEAKEST ELEMENT (medium confidence on its own): the NE quadrant is the duller spring capture and is heavily conifer-shadowed there, so I could not resolve individual pads; the pad given is the guide's line-start with a plausible 22x13 m footprint. There is a smooth pale-green patch at roughly (164..193, -417..-399) that is the likely tee complex. OSM forest w438969919 lies just left (west) of the line between z=-465 and z=-547 and does not intrude on it. No water anywhere near this hole.

Disc 11 sits immediately north of green 10 (48 m walk) and its line runs due west along the top of the banguide, bending gently south, ending at a flag whose pole base falls exactly on OSM green G14 - confirmed by overlaying the G14 marker on the banguide, where the cyan marker lands on the flagpole foot. Par 4, ~373 m, playing WSW (tee bearing 264 deg). The green is flanked by OSM bunkers b44 (long-left, -68.3,-528.7) and b45 (right, -59.8,-502.7); my own trace off a 0.1 m/px crop matched the OSM ring within ~3 m, so the OSM ring is returned. WATER: the boomerang-shaped pond directly short-right of the green is OSM w438967946 (794 m2) and I confirmed its outline against a 0.075 m/px crop point-for-point - it pinches the approach hard, its NW tip reaching z=-502 at x=-27, only ~10 m off the line, which is why my fairway's south edge runs tight along z~-500 for x=-25..8. FAIRWAY: a corridor ~35-40 m wide; the south edge is set by OSM forest w438969919 (its north edge runs z~-545 for x=152..222 - I initially misread this stand as sitting ON the line, but the OSM polygon and a 0.1 m/px re-check put it clear to the south), and the north edge by the scattered tree line and track at z~-600. Fairway starts ~55 m off the tee and stops ~13 m short of the green edge. TEE is medium confidence on its own: the tee-end imagery is the hazy spring capture, full of long conifer shadows; I could not resolve pads, so the single pad is the guide's line-start with a plausible footprint. A straight OSM ditch (w439104649) runs NNW from (344.7,-558.1) about 50 m east of the tee, away from play - not included.

Longest hole of the three: a PAR 5 of ~518 m. Disc 12 is at the far north of the banguide, ~120 m NE of green 11, and its line arcs SW the whole width of the course to a flag at the extreme west end; overlaying the OSM markers on the banguide put the G3 cyan marker exactly on that flagpole's foot, with disc 13 just south of it - so greenOsmIndex 3 is certain. I traced the line through three overlapping 4x banguide crops and matched the pieces at their overlaps, which is how I caught an earlier mis-join with hole 13's parallel line. IMPORTANT ADJUSTMENT: the banguide draws holes as smooth arcs, and here the arc runs 17-40 m WEST of the real mown strip through the middle of the hole (at z=-397 the arc is at x=-319 while the strip between the river and the lake is centred near x=-297). I therefore moved the centerline onto the actual corridor, measured from the river's east bank and the lake's west edge, keeping the guide's tee and green fixed; the length is unchanged at ~518 m. The corridor is a dogleg left, bearing swinging from ~251 deg at the tee to ~224 deg at the green. WATER: two features, both from OSM and both checked against the imagery. The lake (w35415028, 6272 m2, SW tip near -349,-283 running NE to -194,-440) sits 25-45 m off the SE/left side of the closing 250 m - note it lies BETWEEN holes 12 and 13, so hole 13 will legitimately claim it too. The 'ditch' ring is a 7 m-wide ribbon I built along OSM's Hagaan river line (w23074266) where it forms the NW boundary; it passes ~30 m west of the green and makes a sharp eastward elbow at z~-382 that the fairway edge has to skirt (I inserted vertices at (-320,-392) and (-345,-372) for exactly that). FAIRWAY is a single ~45 m corridor from ~55 m off the tee to ~12 m short of the green, hand-trimmed to stay east of the river and west of the lake. TEE medium confidence on its own: the guide's tee point sits on a 45x27 m pale sandy/worn patch at roughly (-32..12, -600..-573) - almost certainly the tee complex on this esker sand, but individual pads are not resolvable at 0.3 m/px, so one representative pad is given.

Par 4, 333 m. Identification: I detected all 18 red flags (green ends) and all numbered discs (tee ends) in the banguide image, then least-squares fitted guide-pixels to world metres on 16 flag/OSM-green pairs. The fit is a pure scale of 0.6536 m/px with 0.1 deg rotation and residuals <= 4.5 m, so the banguide is a plain north-up orthophoto of the same ground. Disc 13 lands at (-400.7,-237.9) and flag 13 lands 0.6 m from OSM green G8 (w452926948). Three independent confirmations: (a) the guide's own drawn hole line, extracted column-by-column from the white pixels, runs tee->green and measures 339 m against the card's 333 m; my 6-point centerline measures 335.8 m (+0.8%); (b) lake w35415028 lies on the LEFT for the whole line, matching the guide note 'Lake the ENTIRE left side, tee to green'; (c) the extracted line bends from bearing 59 deg to 30 deg over the last 60 m, matching 'Bends slightly left near the green'. Tee 13 is a 46 m walk from green 12 (G3) and green 13 is a 70 m walk to tee 14. CAUTION on tees: the Esri z18 imagery is soft here and no crisp pads resolve, so the three pads are placed on the play axis at the card distances 333/321/265 from the guide disc - treat cx/cz as +/-10 m. The terraced tan feature at about (-360,-255), 15 m RIGHT of the line just off the tee, is the shaped mounding the club plan marks START KULLAR / SLUT KULLAR; it is NOT a tee (using it as one would make the hole 285 m). Fairway edges are inferred, not traced: NW edge held 5 m off the surveyed lake shore, SE edge 20 m off the centre line inside the scattered treeline; the corridor runs from 75 m off the tee to 40 m short of the green. Water: the big lake is OSM w35415028 (6272 m2, simplified to 12 points); also included is the 43 m2 ditch pond w438982467 27 m south of the tee - two further OSM ditches (w439046947, stream w439046948) drain SW from there and are not included.

Par 3, 153 m - the second-shortest hole. Identification: banguide disc 14 sits at (-120.8,-505.7) under the same fitted transform used for 13 and 15, and its drawn line is a straight vertical run due SOUTH to the flag, which lands 2.3 m from OSM green G10 (w452926950). The straight tee-green distance is 153.2 m against the card's 153 m - a 0.1% match, the tightest of the three holes, which is what pins the assignment. Routing check: green 13 (G8) is a 70 m walk back to this tee and green 11 (G14, at -74.8,-496.8) is 45 m ENE of it, both normal walks. The hole plays back down the EAST side of the 13th's finish - green 13 is only 27 m west of the line of play, which is tight but is what both sources show. NO WATER anywhere on the hole, matching the guide note. OSM bunkers at (-121.7,-366.4) front-left of the green and (-116,-338) behind-right frame it. CAUTION on tees: no separable pads resolve in the imagery; there is a mown/tan platform with vehicle tracks from about (-122,-535) to (-112,-508), and the three pads given are placed on the axis (x about -116) at the card distances 153/143 (135 shares it) /104 - treat cx/cz as +/-10 m. Fairway: I have given only the mown approach apron in front of the green rather than a tee-to-green corridor, because the ground between tee and green is undifferentiated mown grass carrying scattered specimen trees around x -125..-105, z -420..-385; a par 3 here has no real fairway. Green ring traced from the bright putting surface in a x7 z18 crop; it is a bean/kidney opening to the NW, area 489 m2 against OSM's 555.

Par 4, 337 m, stroke index 2. Identification: banguide disc 15 at (-110.2,-246.2), and the drawn line runs SW to a flag that lands 1.8 m from OSM green G12 (w452926952). The guide line, extracted column-by-column, measures 338.8 m against the card's 337 m; my 5-point centerline measures 338.4 m (+0.4%). Four independent confirmations from the club notes: (a) the line bends LEFT, from bearing 237 deg off the tee to 217 deg into the green ('bends LEFT'); (b) OSM ponds w306287289 and w306287291 sit 20-27 m to the RIGHT of the line, 67-112 m from the green, matching 'Pond RIGHT in the approach zone (67-110 m out)' exactly; (c) the OSM fairway bunker at (-301.4,-123.5) sits on the right edge at the pond corner; (d) hole 8 runs the opposite way 78 m to the right, the intern O/B pair 8/15, and tee 16 is a 50 m walk from this green. The O/B on the LEFT is the driving range: the OSM range polygon's NW boundary runs 3-12 m outside my SE fairway edge and is what bounds the corridor on that side. Tees: a smooth pale pad IS visible at about (-119,-256) in a x7 z18 crop, 15 m from the guide disc, so the back tee complex is real; the three pads given are placed on the play axis at the card distances 337/328 (319 shares it) /224 - treat cx/cz as +/-8 m for the back pair and +/-15 m for the 224 m orange tee, which I could not see. Fairway inferred: 22 m left / 16 m right of the centre line, from 78 m off the tee to 38 m short of the green, with the right edge held 5 m clear of both surveyed ponds. One caveat: a lone tree at (-227,-163) stands about 5 m right of the drawn line, inside my fairway ring - the guide line is schematic to roughly +/-10 m laterally, so the real fairway is probably a few metres further SE there.

Identified from the club banguide: disc 16 sits immediately south of green 15 and east of green 7, and its line runs SE then S to the flag at the bottom-centre. I georeferenced the whole banguide by least-squares fitting the 18 red-flag markers to the 17 OSM green centroids: 16 flags matched 1:1 with residuals 0.15-2.0 m (scale 0.65347 m/px, rotation -0.035 deg), so the banguide is a plain north-up scaled raster and every disc/flag position converts to world metres exactly. GREEN NOT IN OSM: only two of the 18 flags have no OSM green under them, and these are holes 16 and 17 (the one unused OSM green, G1 at (408,353), lies ~470 m east on the club's short course). The banguide-derived pin for 16 lands at (-217.2,423.5); my independent satellite trace of the putting surface centres at (-216.3,424.4) - 1.2 m apart, which is a strong cross-check. Corroborated by all five OSM bunkers here: fairway bunker 32 (-197,141) sits on the right edge of the corridor, and greenside bunkers 25/26/27/28 ring the green I traced. Tees: three mown pads step SE from (-366,14) to (-330,41), the back one exactly on the banguide disc. Card 468 m (black); my centreline measures 475 m. The hole plays ESE off the tee over ~90 m of scrub/rough (guide: BLIND, bell protocol), then turns right into a S-running corridor - a bigger bend (~50 deg) than the guide's 'bends gently RIGHT'. WATER: the guide's 'crossing DIKE at 131 m from the green' (~z=295) is not visible at 0.3 m/px in this spring imagery, so no water traced.

Banguide disc 17 is the southernmost white disc; its line runs NNE to the flag at (-57.1,229.5) via the same 16-point similarity fit described for hole 16.
